title: paid-event.html
content: If you have created a Paid {{variable.Object_Event}} , the following steps will walk you through what an {{variable.Object_Attendee}} sees, and how it looks in your Salesforce org. Create a Unique Checkout Experience Keep in mind, that all colors, images, and text you see are 100% customizable to your specific use case! An {{variable.Object_Attendee}} views your {{variable.Object_Event}} listing. They can click the Share button to generate a URL to share the Event on LinkedIn, X/Twitter, or Facebook, or they can click {{variable.Button_GetTicket}} s to start the process. The {{variable.Object_Attendee}} selects which Tickets ( {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s) and how many they want to purchase and clicks {{variable.Button_Continue}} . Or, if a value is in the Event Item’s {{variable.Field_EVItem_DefaultQtySelecti}} field and the Event Item isn’t sold out or isn’t a Donation, the default quantity of Tickets is automatically added to the cart the first time an Attendee reaches the Event Item selection screen. Attendees can change the number of Tickets in their cart and move around the Event’s webpage without changes being made to their cart based on the default quantity. If the number of remaining tickets is greater than 0 but less than the {{variable.Field_EVItem_DefaultQtySelecti}} , all remaining tickets will be added to the cart. For example, if the number of remaining tickets is 3, but the Default Quantity Selection is “5,” then 3 tickets will be added to the cart. NOTE: When an Attendee purchases Tickets from their AttendeeLink, the default quantity will not be added to the cart. (The original behavior is unchanged.) If an {{variable.Object_Event}} has paid and free Tickets, the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} will see the {{variable.Button_GetTicket}} s button. If the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} only selects the free {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , they will see the {{variable.Button_Register}} button. If they choose a combination of free and paid {{variable.Object_EventItem}} s, they will see the Checkout button. {{variable.Object_Attendee}} s will not see the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} {{variable.Field_ETEventItem_Description}} during checkout if your {{variable.Object_Event}} only has one free Event Item. To add a description of the {{variable.Object_EventItem}} , include the information in the {{variable.Object_Event}} ’s {{variable.Field_ETEvent_Description}} field. {{snippet.EventItem_Checkout10orLess}} The {{variable.Object_Attendee}} enters in their information: {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_LastName}} , {{variable.Field_ETAttendee_FirstName}} , {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} etc. and clicks  {{variable.Button_Continue}} . Everything you see here can be changed as well for a fully customizable checkout, including the language options in the {{variable.Feature_DataDictionary}} . The {{variable.Object_Attendee}} enters any additional contact information and their card details and clicks Place Your Order . The {{variable.Object_Attendee}} receives the {{variable.Field_ETEvent_RegSuccessMsg}} . A thank you message and all the information needed to attend the {{variable.Object_Event}} will be sent to the {{variable.Field_Attendee_Email}} that the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} entered. If your {{variable.Object_Event}} includes {{variable.Object_Session}} s, the following will occur when adding   {{variable.Object_Session}} s during the checkout process. If there are no   {{variable.Field_Session_Track}}   values available, the Track filter will not be visible. If there are no   {{variable.Field_Session_Topic}}   values, the Topic filter will not be visible. The Search Bar will be visible only if there are 20 or more   {{variable.Object_Session}} s to choose from. The "Clear Filter" option will only be available when a value is selected for that filter. Payment Security Payments and card data are securely processed and are PCI compliant. Salesforce users can view the related {{variable.Object_Attendee}} information. Financial summaries and totals are immediately updated with related payments or as we call them, Invoices . Check out the out-of-the-box Event financial report for quick summaries on your completed {{variable.Object_Event}} !
